title: Site Safety When Building a House in 2027: Who Does What
desc: Worker safety when building a house in 2027: duties of owner, contractor and workers; danger zones, scaffolding, electricity, insurance and accident response.
summary: Allocation of occupational safety responsibility between owner, contractor and workers when building a private house, and what to do when an accident occurs on site.
body: p

Falls from height, electric shocks and scaffolding collapses are not rare on private house sites. When they happen, the first question is who is responsible. This article summarises the rules on occupational safety in house construction under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 207/2026/ND-CP. (Fines for screening and environmental hygiene are covered in the article Fines for safety and screening violations when building a house.)
h2
1. Responsibilities of the house owner
ul

For a private house, the house owner organises construction, supervises construction and is responsible for safety during construction, including adjacent works and the environment (Point b, Clause 3, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026).

What the owner needs to supervise: construction methods, safety measures for their own house and the adjoining houses; the scaffolding system, temporary supporting structures, machinery and equipment; and general safety measures (Clause 4, Article 10).

The investor may suspend construction and require the contractor to remedy breaches of safety rules (Point c, Clause 1, Article 59 of the Construction Law); must organise supervision of the contractor's compliance with safety rules, coordinate in handling accidents and promptly notify the state authority of any fatal occupational accident (Clause 2, Article 51).
h2
2. Responsibilities of the construction contractor
ul
Ensure occupational safety and hygiene; safety of the works, assets, equipment and vehicles; and fire prevention and fighting (Clause 1, Article 51 of the Construction Law).

Identify danger zones in construction, prepare safety measures for these zones and submit them to the investor for approval, and review them periodically and when unforeseen events occur (Clause 3, Article 51).
Machinery and equipment with strict safety requirements must be inspected before use (Clause 5, Article 51).
The contractor's safety officer must be trained in occupational safety or construction engineering (Clause 5, Article 15 of Decree 207/2026).
Buy insurance for workers on the site and third-party civil liability insurance (Point c, Clause 1, Article 10 of the Construction Law).
h2
3. Rights and responsibilities of workers
p

Under Article 17 of Decree 207/2026, workers must comply with safety rules; report hazards when they find them; may refuse work they consider unsafe or where they are not given adequate personal protective equipment; and may take on work with strict safety requirements only after being trained and issued a safety card.
h2
4. Common danger points on private house sites
ul
Working at height: floor edges, stairwells and light wells without temporary guardrails; workers not wearing safety harnesses.
Scaffolding: makeshift footings, missing bracing, rotten floor boards; bracing removed for easier passage.
Construction electricity: bare wires, temporary splices, no shock-protection devices, cables lying in water.
Machinery: cutting machines and mixers without guards; hoists lifting materials without checks on the cable and brake.
Deep excavations: unsupported walls, next to the neighbouring house.
h2
5. What to do when an accident occurs
ol
Give first aid and take the injured person to emergency care; stop the related work and leave the scene undisturbed within the limits of safety.

The contractor must stop construction when there is a risk of, or has been, an accident; failing to stop may be fined from VND 10–20 million (minor injury) to VND 60–80 million (death or serious injury) – these are the amounts for organisations (Point e, Clause 1 and Point c, Clause 4, Article 23 of Decree 339/2026).

Notify the competent state authority when there is a fatal accident (Clause 2, Article 51 of the Construction Law). Reporting and investigating occupational accidents follow the law on occupational safety and hygiene (Article 49 of Decree 207/2026).
p

note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal texts. Fines under Decree 339/2026/ND-CP are those applicable to organisations; for individuals the amount is half (Clause 4, Article 5).
